title: What ZIA Terraform data sources return, drop, or get wrong
aliases: zia data source fails to read
zia data source empty result no error

prose.text: A ZIA data source is supposed to be a faithful read-only view of an object. In the provider it is a hand-written pair of a schema and a flattener, fed by an SDK model, and the three drift apart in a few repeatable ways. When a data source gives a surprising answer, compare the schema, the flattener and the SDK model before suspecting the tenant (the write-side version of this is in [[zia.terraform.field-fidelity]]).

checks.do: Whether the failing object has the shape that triggers a flattener failure, before concluding the data source is broken on every tenant.
Whether the two selectors given to a data source agree, since the first matching entry is returned.
Which policy criteria a rule read through a data source is missing, starting with the URL filtering, traffic capture and location data sources.
Whether an empty attribute is never set: search the data source file for its snake_case key, where one hit, in the schema, means it is never set.

sandbox-rss-signature-sources-scalar-in-.statement: In the sandbox report data source, each risk/signature entry declares `signature_sources` as a `TypeSet`, but the SDK field it is filled from is a single `string`, and the flattener assigns that string directly into the map handed to `d.Set`.

upstream.note: Filing 15 (ZIA data sources) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sandbox-rss-scalar-set-panics.statement: Writing a scalar string into a nested `TypeSet` through `d.Set` makes the Terraform plugin SDK panic on a failed type assertion instead of returning an error, so a sandbox report that has any spyware, networking, security-bypass, exploit, stealth or persistence entry can crash the provider process during the read. This applies only when `details = "full"`, the only branch that flattens the RSS.
sandbox-rss-scalar-set-panics.conditions: Depends on terraform-plugin-sdk v2.40.1, which is not vendored in this repository. Read from the module source (helper/schema/field_writer_map.go, MapFieldWriter.setSet): a non-slice value skips the slice-to-Set conversion and reaches `value.(*Set)`, an unchecked assertion. Not executed. The panic also needs a report whose RSS lists are non-empty, which depends on what the sandbox returns.

upstream.note: Filing 15 (ZIA data sources) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

gre-vip-negative-required-count-slices.statement: `required_count` in the GRE VIP recommendation data source has a default of 5 and no validation. After the SDK call the code compares the list length with it and slices `[:requiredCount]`, so a negative value always passes the comparison and reaches the slice expression.

undeclared-key-write-errors.statement: A checked `d.Set` that receives a key the schema does not declare returns an error, and these data sources return it as a diagnostic, so the whole read fails. Because the failing key is emitted per element, the data source fails only for responses that actually contain such an element (a populated excluded list, an ECZPA segment, a `managed_by` object, an EDM mapping, a CBI profile, a proxy gateway), and works on tenants whose objects are empty. The browser control data source is the exception to any data dependence: its two undeclared top-level keys fail whenever the API responds.
undeclared-key-write-errors.conditions: Depends on terraform-plugin-sdk v2.40.1, which is not vendored. Read from the module source (helper/schema/field_writer_map.go): MapFieldWriter returns `Invalid address to set` when the schema lookup for a key is empty, and setObject propagates the error of each nested key. Not executed. Whether real responses contain the triggering objects is server data.

gre-vip-false-zero-inverted.statement: Because `GetOk` reports an explicit `false` or `0` as not set, `within_country_only = false` is never sent and the SDK then requests `true`, the opposite of the configured value; zero latitude or longitude is dropped the same way.
gre-vip-false-zero-inverted.conditions: Depends on terraform-plugin-sdk v2 `GetOk` treating a zero value as unset; the module is not vendored in this repository, so no captured source states it.

gre-vip-negative-count-panics.statement: A negative `required_count` makes that slice expression panic, crashing the provider during the read.
gre-vip-negative-count-panics.conditions: Go rejects a negative slice bound at run time with a panic; that is language behaviour, not stated in any captured source.

nonnumeric-or-empty-id-outcome.title: What the plugin SDK and Terraform do with a data source that finishes with an empty ID, or a non-integer ID on an integer `id`
nonnumeric-or-empty-id-outcome.blocks: saying whether the devices empty-result path, the GRE VIP read without `source_ip`, and the multi-result endpoint tag read return an error, an empty state, or a state build failure
nonnumeric-or-empty-id-outcome.detail: The code facts are certain: the devices data source returns without an ID when the device list is empty, the GRE VIP read sets an empty ID when source_ip is omitted, and the endpoint tag read sets a channel name as the ID of a schema whose `id` is an integer. What follows depends on terraform-plugin-sdk v2.40.1 (ResourceData.State returns nil for an empty ID; State reads every schema key through its type reader, and ResourceData.get panics on a reader error) and on Terraform core. Neither is vendored here and the behavior was read, not executed. Resolve with a provider test that runs each read against a fake SDK response and records the diagnostics and state.

api-response-shape-for-flattener-failure.title: Whether real ZIA responses contain the objects that trigger the flattener failures and phantom blocks
api-response-shape-for-flattener-failure.blocks: saying how often the read failures, the sandbox panic and the empty blocks actually occur
api-response-shape-for-flattener-failure.detail: Every claim about a failing or phantom flatten depends on a response containing a populated excluded list, an extensions map, an ECZPA segment, a managedBy object, an EDM mapping, a CBI profile, RSS entries, or on the API omitting a value-typed sub-object. The client code shows what happens if so; the server's responses are not shown by code. Resolve with scratch-tenant reads of each object type, or recorded API responses. Browser control needs no test: its undeclared top-level keys fail on every read.
